            self.health = health
            self.direction = direction
            self.index = index
    def survivedRobotsHealths(self, positions: List[int], healths: List[int], directions: str) -> List[int]:

        vals = [self.Robot(positions[i], healths[i], directions[i], i) for i in range(n)]

                gone = True
            if not gone:
                stack.append(robot)
        stack.sort(key=lambda x: x.index)
        return [robot.health for robot in stack]

let last_robot = &mut robots[last_idx]; let current_robot = &mut robots[i];
You created two mutable references at the same time, &mut robots[...] Pointing to the same Vec is illegal in Rust's borrowing rules (even if the two indexes are different, Rust cannot statically guarantee non-overlap at compile time).
Furthermore, stack.last() only returns immutable references (&usize), and you internally modified robots[last_idx], which leads to the contradiction of "simultaneous mutable and immutable borrowing". Please modify through temporarily retrieve the index and separate the mutable reference with scope.
